request.spec:
A claim with a negative amount is a correction. It is allowed only when the claim form names, by
number, a SETTLED claim of the same person that it corrects; otherwise it is refused. A
correction's due is its amount times the rate, rounded like any claim, with no floor and no late
charge. It is numbered, opened and settled like any claim, counts in every total, and shows the
number it corrects.

You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim with a negative amount is a correction. It is allowed only when the claim form names, by
number, a SETTLED claim of the same person that it corrects; otherwise it is refused. A
correction's due is its amount times the rate, rounded like any claim, with no floor and no late
charge. It is numbered, opened and settled like any claim, counts in every total, and shows the
number it corrects.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Corrections are in place, and `bin/e2e` passes, three runs out of three.

**How it works now**
- **Adding a correction:** the claim form has a new "Corrects claim number" field (`claim-form-corrects`). Any claim with a negative amount must name a SETTLED claim of the same person by its number. If it doesn't, the server refuses it, the form shows `claim-form-error`, and nothing is stored or audited. The screen only checks that a number was typed; the server decides whether that claim is settled, because the screen may be out of date when someone else has just settled it.
- **Its due:** amount × rate, rounded half-to-even like any claim, with no floor and no late charge. This applies both when it is settled and to its live due on screen, including the due total when a period is closed (`PeriodService`). Negative amounts now format correctly, so -0.30 displays as `-0.30`.
- **Everything else** works as for any claim: it's numbered when opened, can be settled, counts in every total, and shows the number it corrects in `claim-corrects`.
- **Storage:** migration `V24__claim_correction.sql` adds a `corrects` column. It also rebuilds `amount` without its old "0 or more" check, because H2 gave that check an automatic name and can't drop it any other way.

**A loading fix you should know about:** the first test run failed because of a timing gap. After the sheet was re-loaded, the sheet id appeared before the people and claims were read back, so the test counted 0 claims and then took the reloaded ones as "added". I added a small counter in `core/session.ts` so the sheet id only appears once people, claims, rates, periods and roles have all been read again. This changes when every panel shows as loaded, not just claims.

**Choices I made where the request was silent:**
- A positive amount ignores any number typed in the corrects field.
- The quick-add bar still only takes amounts of 0 or more, since it has nowhere to name a claim to correct.
- An open correction past its due date still counts as overdue; it just never gets a late charge.
